lessons: In invalid_output_exhausted, move the request-count and re-prompt-text assertions out of the FakeLLM diagnosis callable. Run them after `await bench.drain()`. If one is raised inside llm_call, Driver.run swallows it as infra_error and the member stays green whatever the driver does.

Filter bench.llm.requests to `ticket == stem and surface == 'implement'`, since the diagnose request also carries the stem. Assert the count equals `bench.config.caps.retry + 1`, and assert that every re-prompt after the first contains the prior `[invalid_artifact]` finding line.

Script the diagnosis as a plain string reply, not a callable. Assert that the harvested diagnosis signal is not mechanical (no infra_error or abandon-human fallback), so a swallowed exception can no longer turn the member green.

Check each member's assertions by temporarily breaking the observable (for example, an off-by-one in the expected count) and confirming the member goes red. Then restore it. A member that cannot fail is the reject condition.
Keep the eval/shakeout/bench.py diff to wiring the bench clock into the Checkout sleep seam. The ticket rules out any other bench edit. Do not commit the generated shakeout-report.json.
